newsitem.title: UK: Copper concludes LME above $1,950, helps aluminium.
newsitem.headline: Copper concludes LME above $1,950, helps aluminium.

text.p: Copper prices pushed above $1,950 during Thursday afternoon LME trading, with the firmer trend assisting the aluminium market in recovering from early fresh 2-1/2 year lows.

Traders said short-term technical tightness on the LME helped copper break back above $1,950, with November and December dates in keen demand. This expanded the overall cash/threes spread out to around $15 backwardation from $8 on Wednesday.

The tightness reflects a finely balanced short-term supply/demand picture, with LME warehouse inventories expected to fall again on Friday. If the current upturn is maintained the next objective is the crucial $1,970 level. Last trade on the kerb was at $1,958 a tonne, up $30 from Wednesday's kerb.

Copper's rally, as well as short-term oversold warnings, helped aluminium recover from midmorning blues when prices slumped to new 2-1/2 year lows of $1,305 when investment banks and speculators lined up to sell.
The expected short-covering helped prices recover and move back up to $1,332 a tonne, a $9 gain on the day, although a test of $1,300 is expected in the not-too-distant future.
IPAI producer stocks rose marginally in August, but more pertinently LME warehouse stocks are likely to register an increase on Friday.
Nickel prices managed to recover from under $7,100 - a level seen as short-term technical support - with the market pushing above $7,200 to settle at $7,220, up $90 from Wednesday.
However, traders still expect prices to retreat and test $7,000 at some stage, with inventories on a rising trend at present. Stocks are seen higher on Friday, they said.

The zinc market recovered from its midsession wobble down to near $1,030, helped by copper, and prices edged back up to close the session at $1,033, down just $2 with the market comfortable in a $1,030/40 jobbing range.
Lead trading was slow throughout the day, and the market stayed glued to overnight levels. Three months finished indicated at a little changed $766/67 a tonne.
Tin business was lacklustre, although prices were adjusted higher during the afternoon in line with copper. Three months finished at $6,070/75, up from Wednesday's close of $6,055.
There was little interest in alloy, although prices inched higher with primary to finish at $1,200, up $5.
